projects.name: RobCo
projects.overview: Project Overview Following the success of our brand evolution for RobCo, we were commissioned to create a 3D motion piece that brought their four core brand messages to life. Through immersive visuals and thoughtful storytelling, we transformed these messages into a dynamic animation that reflects RobCo’s innovative spirit and values. Services Storyboarding 3D Modelling Motion Design Date September, 2024 Client RobCo Location Berlin, Germany Initial Concepts We began by developing an animatic and sketches to outline the overall approach and narrative we aimed to convey in this project. Toggle Sound Modular The first theme we focused on visualising was the idea of modularity. As the robots can be configured in numerous ways, we aimed to convey the idea of individual modules coming together in a smooth motion before connecting to reveal the final form of the RobCo robot. 1 /5 Prev Next Easy The second chapter of the animation highlighted the ease of using the robots. Through the native RobCo software and app, users can quickly and effortlessly configure the robots to carry out various tasks. To showcase this, we designed a stylised interface that depicted the simple drag and drop nature of the software in a more visually engaging form. 1 /5 Prev Next Adaptable Adaptability was another core theme we needed to convey in the video – the robots’ ability to be configured for various environments and equipped with different attachments to suit specific use cases. To illustrate this, we depicted the robot in three common scenarios with sleek cuts between each scene to enhance the visual flow. 1 /5 Prev Next Autonomous The final chapter focused on autonomy and the advanced smart technology within the robots, which utilises AI to organise and manage fleets efficiently. To convey this concept, we designed a scan-reveal effect that alludes to the robot’s complex inner workings and showcased smart features such as part scanning and detection. 1 /10 Prev Next From the client “The animation produced by Unseen seamlessly brought our USPs, key messaging, and core values to life through a show-stopping motion piece that serves as a cornerstone in how we communicate our story. projects.name: KIKK 2024
projects.overview: Project Overview For the second year running we took on the exciting challenge of designing the KIKK festival branding for the 2024 edition of the event. Services Brand Identity Motion Design Website Design Date October, 2024 Client KIKK Location Namur, Belgium True/False Can we still believe in visuals? Can we distinguish between true and false in the digital era and the development of generative AI? These were the questions that the KIKK team posed to us when briefing in the theme for the 2024 edition of the festival; True/False. Our response to this both challenging and exciting brief was to create a visual direction that explored the idea of distorting reality and presenting these 2 versions in a slick animated identity. Process: Generative Visual Exploration During the initial phases of the project we experimented with a number of techniques to create the distorted graphical representations, including generative code based tools built in WebGL, touch designer visuals and traditional 3d graphics. A Unique Touch As with all our projects, we strive to explore new technologies and integrate them into our workflows. During our initial exploration of techniques for creating the distorted visuals, we found that the results produced in TouchDesigner were really promising. Embracing this potential, we developed a process to generate unique visuals using simple gradients, 3D assets or even the webcam feed as inputs, generating a dynamic and interactive point field which would be used to drive the distortion of an evolving gradient, creative a for a unique and pattern with each generation. From the client “The KIKK Festival 2024 visual identity perfectly reflects this year’s thematic focus while embracing the festival’s unique, bold, and crazy spirit. It brilliantly captures the energy and creativity that make KIKK so special, turning our vision into a dynamic visual experience that truly resonates with our community.” Marie du Chastel, KIKK Festival Next Nikolas Type (Keep Scrolling) Drag to explore our world Selected Projects Filter All Branding Digital Motion Experiment View our work Say hello we look forward to hearing from you New Business General ⮡   hello@unseen.co Bristol 35a Colston Avenue Bristol, BS1 4TT London 90 Paul Street London, EC2A 4NE ⮡   projects@unseen.c

projects.name: Seascape Survey
projects.overview: Project Overview An immersive educational experience to increase awareness around the oceans role in carbon storage. Services WebGL 3D Design Digital Strategy UI & UX Design Augmented Reality Web XR View project Date January, 2020 Client Blue Marine & Convex Location London, UK Process Snapshot A look at some of the initial concept work that went into creating the projects scrolling narrative. Project Objectives The Convex Seascape Survey is an ambitious 4 year research programme, investigating and quantifying carbon storage in coastal seas around the globe. The website is an introduction to the concept of seascape carbon storage and the role we believe the ocean plays. The immersive experience is the first piece of a larger campaign that will span the next 3 years. The core objective for this phase of the campaign was raising awareness and understanding around carbon storage in our oceans. Our aim was to educate a broad segment of the general public and help them understand the importance of the topic and the need for research around it. Creating the narrative With such a complex subject and and broad target audience the challenge was explaining the science in an accessible way, using plain language and a logical narrative flow to guide the user on an educational journey, without overwhelming them with unnecessary content and scientific jargon. For a deeper insight into the process behind creating this immersive website follow the link below. Learn More Integrated AR experience The AR easter egg was integrated into the website to add another layer of immersion for the user to experience along the journey. The experience was created as part of a larger educational campaign. We also created a virtual reality experience taking you on a journey to discover what a healthy ocean looks like. The campaign We created the immersive AR experience for World Ocean Day which allowed users to walk with whales and encouraged them to share their experience on social media using the hashtag #walkwithwhales to raise awareness for ocean health. The results The campaign was a huge success with over 4.5 Million people reached, and people all around the globe sharing their own ‘Walk With Whales’ experience. projects.name: Crosswire
projects.overview: Project Overview We created an identity for Crosswire and developed a website that truly sets them apart from their competitors. Services Branding Digital WebGL View project Date January, 2020 Client Crosswire Location New York, USA Concept Exploration Some early iterations of the core visual narrative and art direction. Creating the digital landscape Crosswire challenged us to create a website that defied conventions; something that fully embodied their disruptive approach to the industry. It needed to be unique, memorable and visually striking. The core challenge was visualising Crosswire’s complex service offering in a simple and digestible way. Our solution was to create a 3D environment that represented the digital landscape of a customer’s business which we then brought to life using WebGL. Concept and execution The environment was designed using a 3D grid system, inspired by the shapes that make up the company’s brand mark. By repeating these components, we created sections and simple animations to work as visual representations of the product features. The small triangular shapes that move around the landscape represent the users of the product. If you’re interested in knowing a bit more about how we created these features you can read our technical case study for some more in-depth insights into our process. Technical Case Study Creating the brand We created a brand identity to accurately reflect Crosswire’s values and approach to access management. This included a core brand mark; which is recognisable and nuanced, creative display type echoing the brands visual metaphors, a suite of 2D and 3D brand assets, collateral, website and a comprehensive set of guidelines to help Crosswire scale their brand as their product evolves. projects.name: Blue Marine
projects.overview: Project Overview An immersive educational experience created for Blue Marine Foundation, one of the world’s leading marine preservation charities Services WebGL UX/UI Digital Strategy 3D Motion Design CGI View project Date Winter, 2021 Client Blue Marine Foundation Location London, UK Concept Ideation We initially explored a number of possible art directions for the project, along with exploring various interactive ideas and concepts. The challenge Blue Marine Foundation challenged us to create a digital experience that successfully educates people on the importance of our oceans and the solutions we can implement to mitigate climate change. The health of the ocean affects us all and for that reason, the site needed to connect with as many people as possible, from students to policymakers. The journey begins with an introduction to ocean preservation, in the form of a meditative breathing exercise. This aims to reduce tension and in-turn improve concentration and memory. The site then submerges users into 3 unique and realistic underwater worlds using interactive 3D environments and engaging user interface to create a holistic learning experience, capture data and inspire action. View Experience The project focuses on 3 core topics; sustainable fishing, blue carbon habitats and marine protected areas The Sea We Breathe is an immersive educational experience, which aims to raise awareness, inspire action and help in the preservation of our oceanic ecosystems. The project focuses on 3 core topics; sustainable fishing, blue carbon habitats and marine protected areas. Each topic is brought to life through an interactive underwater journey narrated by the wonderful Stephen Fry. The goal was to encapsulate the users through highly engaging multi-sensory adventures, helping to create lasting emotional connections with the information they discover. Blue Carbon Habitats Each journey takes you through a unique underwater environment. ‘Rainforest Of The Sea’ focuses on blue carbon habitats using the waters surrounding the Maldives as its canvas. The journeys contain an abundance of educational content weaved into cohesive narratives. There are unique interactive elements designed to engage the user as they explore each environment. View Journey Marine Protected Areas The second journey ‘Protecting The Underwater World’ focuses on marine protected areas in the deep blue waters of The Atlantic Ocean. It was important that the narrative inspired positive change rather than focussing on the negative issues. It was this approach that inspired the threat sections of each journey where the user plays an active role in solving the issue using their mouse gestures. View Journey Sustainable Fishing The final journey, ‘The Ocean’s Web Of Life’ is set in the murky water of The North Sea and focuses on sustainable fishing. Along each journey we positioned a number of interactive questions in order to measure user engagement and success of the educational content. View Journey Technical challenges and innovations Recreating the natural world in 3D is notoriously difficult especially with the added restrictions that come with building for the web. Performance had to be considered at all times when designing and building this experience. Lighting and textures played a huge role in the visual quality of the experience. Multiple techniques where used to achieve the final polished look and feel. projects.overview: Project Overview We helped internationally renowned architecture firm CLOU reimagine their digital online presence Services UX & UI Design Digital Design WebGL View project Date May, 2022 Client CLOU Architects Location Beijing, Shanghai & Shenzhen Initial Explorations A collection of early ideas generated at the very beginning of the project, some of which led us to the final outcome. Concept Development CLOU wanted an innovative way to display their work. It needed to be visually impressive but most importantly, functional. It was this key desire that led to the development of the project ring, which sits at the epicentre of the website. Geometric project carousel We knew we had to elevate this core feature beyond a two-dimensional scrolling experience. We wanted to create something memorable, something innovative. Inspired by the physical nature of the architectural world, we began to conceptualise how we might combine project imagery and 3D geometry to create a more digitally tactile interface. The resulting 3D interface is able to handle a large number of project images, something that would have been impossible to achieve in a more traditional approach. In addition, the ring tells a deeper story, becoming an interactive data visualisation that enables users to glean comparative insights into the specialisms and nuances of CLOU’s projects, from genre and scale to status and scope. Bilingual design considerations A major consideration was the bilingual requirements of the site. It needed to look good with both English or Chinese characters. Therefore, while designing we layed out two versions of the site in tandem to ensure this was well considered throughout the design process. projects.name: Blue Marine XR
projects.overview: Project Overview Working with Blue Marine Foundation we created an educational campaign centred around an immersive, virtual reality experience. Services VR AR Instagram Filter Houdini View project Date June, 2023 Client Blue Marine & Convex Location London, UK A virtual reality experience aimed to educate and inspire Introducing “The Sea We Breathe” a virtual reality experience explaining the carbon capture capabilities of the ocean in beautifully immersive 360°, narrated by none other than Helena Bonham Carter. The experience was designed to debut at COP28 and will be used as an educational tool moving forward, allowing people to dive beneath the waves and learn about our planet’s incredible underwater world. Crafting the visual narrative Working closely with the client we created a succinct script for the experience. The core idea revolved around the user visiting three visually distinct underwater locations. The next step was crafting the visual narrative starting with quick sketch work to create a storyboard for each environment. This step was crucial for kick-starting the R&D process and providing the client with a clear vision of our proposed direction. Designing compositions and visual choreography is always challenging in virtual reality and so it was essential we were able to begin prototyping as soon as possible. Research & Development This included optimising scenes for 360-degree views, achieving a realistic look for underwater environments that balanced quality with shorter rendering times, and selecting simulations that would authentically convey the natural movement of species underwater. As well as scene compositions and direction of elements within the scene to ensure the user always had something to look at relevant to the narration. Final Result In order to reach the largest audience possible we built the experience to be accessible not only on VR headsets but on desktop, tablet and mobile devices also. The experience was however optimised for the Meta Quest. In the final product users are invited to immerse themselves in 3 detailed ocean habitats, observe the native sealife up close while learning about important fact about our oceans carbon capture capabilities. Walk With Whales – AR Campaign Working with The Blue Marine Foundation we created an AR campaign for World Ocean Day which allowed users to walk with whales and encouraged them to share their experience on social media using the hashtag #walkwithwhales to raise awareness for ocean health. Try It Out The campaign We launched the campaign for World Ocean Day to raise awareness for ocean health using a fun, interactive and shareable mechanic. The resuts The campaign was a huge success with over 4.5 Million people reached, and people all around the globe sharing their own ‘Walk With Whales’ experience. projects.name: Lewa House
projects.overview: Project Overview An immersive brand experience created for Lewa House, Kenya’s leading wildlife conservancy Services Branding Website CGI View project Date Spring, 2022 Client Lewa House Location Kenya Initial Exploration A round up of our initial concept submissions with many elements from each direction making it into the final design. We created a contemporary new look for Lewa House, while carefully preserving its rustic and authentic charm The full scope of this project involved a total rethink of the Lewa House identity and online presence. We worked closely with the Lewa House team to evolve their brand, maintaining the essence of what makes Lewa so special, whilst giving it a more contemporary feel in order to appeal to a wider audience. Along with creating a new logo mark and introducing a more refined suite of typography, we carefully selected a new set of brand colours featuring warm and earthy tones, inspired by the vibrant Lewa landscape. This was supported by hand drawn elements to add to the rugged charm of the brand, which aimed to emulate the unique experience they offer as a travel destination. An immersive storytelling experience that encourages users to explore the wonders Lewa has to offer We created an explorative journey for users to discover Lewa’s wonders in a nonlinear, organic way. The site still contains a more traditional navigation, allowing users to quickly access information if needed, but the main flow aims to lead users on an exciting, meandering path of discovery. Guided by Sophie, the lodge owner, users are taken on a journey of discovery; learning about Lewa’s history and deep connection to the wildlife they protect. Bringing Lewa’s story to life was our number one priority. We created a highly interactive narrative that ran through the site making use of purposeful animation, gamified features, and rich media. Visit Site The Lewa landscape brought to life through an immersive 3D experience The interactive map sits at the epicentre of the journey, encouraging users to engage with the content on a deeper, more emotional level. Main page links are positioned among educational and informative content which can all be viewed without leaving the map. Explore Map Generating the terrain There were two main challenges when creating Lewa’s map. We first needed to create the 3D geometry of the land using limited topographic data, and next we needed to create an accurate texture for the terrain ensuring the plains, rivers and forest were all represented accurately. Satellite imagery of Lewa was basic, so we utilised Gaea world generator and Substance Painter to build on the data we did have and procedurally added detail to the geometry and texture. The map was then built in WebGL and uses the tiled 4k texture we created custom. Responsive With mobile browsing dominating the tourism industry, particular attention was paid to perfecting performance and functionality on handheld devices. & Immersive Even on these devices the interactive map offers an immersive and memorable way to discover the unique experiences Lewa has to offer. projects.overview: Project Overview A striking pre-launch marketing site for productivity tool of the future; Superlist Services UX/UI DESIGN FRONT-END WEBGL 3D MODELLING View project Date Spring, 2021 Client Superlist Location Berlin, Germany Using 3D visual metaphors to showcase the Superlist product enabled us to say a lot by showing a little Creating excitement and intrigue for the release of Superlist without revealing any specific product features posed an interesting challenge. Our solution was to create bespoke 3D graphics to visualise the core concepts that were then embedded in the site using WebGL, tied to the users scroll position to create a fun and immersive experiences. Toggle Sound All in the details From WebGL 3D buttons complete with sound effects to letter by letter text animations; every detail was carefully considered to provide an extra layer of delight to the interactions that tied in with the fun and friendly Superlist brand feel. Under the hood; technologies and optimisation Matching great creative ideas with equally innovative development techniques is at the heart of our process. The mixture of 3D assets and front-end animations required some outside-of-the-box thinking to ensure optimum performance and load times. For example, we created a custom tool in Houdini that enabled us to remove any faces in the 3D models that weren’t visible; resulting in a much smaller file size and cleaner geometry. Combined with baked-in animations and lightweight matcap texture files, the result is a highly performant scroll experience. These dreamy, surreal images aimed to capture the simple things we missed during periods of self isolation, providing a small moment of relaxed escapism for the viewer. Overgrown A surreal visualisation series, exploring the integration of nature with interiors and architectural spaces. The visuals are a jovial view on what remote working might look like in the future, by placing work stations in dream locations — the ideal workcation! projects.name: BlueYard
projects.overview: Project Overview A futuristic and immersive interactive portfolio for BlueYard, an investment firm funding the next generation of leading tech brands Services WebGL Development Digital Design Brand Evolution Motion Graphics 3D Imagery View project Date Winter, 2021 Client Blue Yard Location Berlin Initial Exploration A selection of early work, exploring different visual representations of BlueYard’s core message – The Fabric of our Future. Over 30,000 particles make up this bespoke nebula This site acts as an immersive portfolio experience that showcases the future-thinking ethos of BlueYard and the companies they invest in, along with positioning them as leaders in the space. On entering, users find themselves floating in the BlueYard galaxy, with clusters representing the different industries they invest in. At the core of the experience is a bespoke nebula particle system that acts as the navigation to inner pages and establishes the core visual aesthetic. This futuristic look immediately sets the tone for what users can expect from the brand and ties in directly with BlueYard’s forward thinking approach. A brand evolution for a revolutionary business Building on the visuals that we created for the BlueYard web experience, we also designed a number of brand assets to be used across social media, pitch decks and other brand collateral. This allowed us to take the concepts and techniques that we explored during the creation of the website and develop them into high-fidelity 3D renders. Technical innovations Building such a rich immersive experience did not come without technical challenges; complex particle animations and detailed embedded 3D models meant we had to come up with new and innovative techniques across both design and development phases to ensure the site runs performantly. A deep-rooted collaboration between 3D design and WebGL development allowed us to establish a custom workflow that enabled us to export complex particle based animations easily from Houdini as compressed image textures. On top of this, we also created a custom export format that could be imported into a WebGL environment resulting in 3D geometry with particle mapping and animation settings. projects.name: Letter
projects.overview: Project Overview Elegant brand visuals and digital showcase for the world’s most exclusive banking platform Services CGI Website Design Development View project Date Winter, 2020 Client Letter Location San Diego, USA Initial Ideation Early conceptual work, exploring 3D brand assets and directions for the interactive experience. When the look is almost as good as the touch Using a combination of high-fidelity pre-rendered visuals and an embedded interactive WebGL model, we gave users a taste of the quality they can expect from Letter’s solid aluminium bank card. A visual breakdown When it came to creating the interactive crystal elements for the website, we had a choice to make. Using live 3D models and textures in WebGL would have created a more interactive experience, but the visuals would have been limited by performance constraints. As aesthetics were central to the brand’s ethos, we opted for a pre-rendered image sequence tied to scroll. This option allowed us to create a high-fidelity visual while retaining an element of user interaction. Brand visuals Building on the high-end aesthetic established on the website, we created beautiful 3D static and motion assets for use across marketing collateral and beyond. projects.name: Dala
projects.overview: Project Overview Creating the brand and online presence for Dala, a groundbreaking AI search tool Services Branding CGI Website Design WebGL Development View project Date Winter, 2021 Client Dala Location London, UK Initial Exploration A selection of early work, exploring different visual representations of Dala’s core brand mission – organising fragmented knowledge. Creating a brand with meaning Dala’s exists to unify fragmented workplace knowledge with its cutting-edge search AI, turning your business files into a hive mind. When creating the brand, we drew inspiration from this central idea, and the mark acts as a visual metaphor for this core theme. We used fragmented shapes drawn together to form a stylised ‘D’ and when rotated, the shape resembles a brain. This theme was then extended through Dala’s visual language and communication, resulting in a meaningful and cohesive brand identity. Finding the perfect visual representation for Dala’s cutting edge service The ideation phase of a project is a time to experiment both visually and conceptually in order to find that unique idea. When it came to creating Dala’s online experience, we focused on the core theme of ‘fragmented knowledge’ while also experimenting with art direction and interaction design. Piecing together the story We created a WebGL particle system for Dala which sits at the epicentre of the website. We use these fragments as a perpetual storytelling device, morphing them to form different visual metaphors as the user navigates down the page.
